rationale: The closest spec, dashboard-variables-refresh.spec.js, exercises the global refresh button + trackPanelReload machinery but every test gates the refresh behind a *dashboard variable* change (a variable is added and mutated before clicking refresh; its tag is @dashboardVariables). This feature is about a *pure* relative-time refresh: a fresh dashboard (default relative 15m, no variables) re-resolves [now-15m, now] when the user clicks refresh, and the subtle span-comparison fix that prevents spurious refetch on non-forced recompute. The panel-time specs (dashboard-panel-time-*) cover panel-level time config and priority, not the global relative-refresh-advances-now behavior. None of them cover a relative-only dashboard whose period string stays 15m while the resolved now advances. That is a distinct feature area (its own slug + run-context spec_path), so a new spec is the least-duplicative action; it reuses the existing ingestion/create/refresh/track helpers rather than re-inventing them.
